To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chromosomal assignment of 63 human brain ESTs was determined by analyzing PCR products amplified with primers designed from the ESTs.

we used PCR and fluorescent detection to localize 67 cDNAs to human chromosomes and to refine the localization of one previously reported assignment, and to localize one human cDNA in the mouse genome.
we have identified 63 novel human chromosome assignments for brain expressed sequence tags and have refined the assignment of 4 other brain ESTs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genes expressed in the human central nervous system.
the development and application of PCR-based chromosome mapping methods.
the identification and characterization of genes that may be important in the pathogenesis of neurologic disease and in the development and maintenance of brain function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human genome contains a minimum of 63 different genes expressed in brain tissue.
the 63 cDNAs were assigned to 22 human chromosomes, including 10 subregions, and 2 mouse chromosomes, and that 1 cDNA was assigned to the Xp11-->p21.2 region.
the 63 human brain ESTs analyzed in this report were assigned to 20 different human chromosomes, with 13 ESTs assigned to specific subregions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
63 of 67 human brain ESTs have been mapped to individual human chromosomes by PCR analysis of hybrid cell panels.
63 of the 73 human brain cDNAs tested in this study were assigned to individual human autosomes, with 13 subregionally localized.
63 ESTs were assigned to individual human and/or mouse chromosomes, and 13 of these were homologues of previously mapped sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human brain is a rich source of novel cDNA sequences, and that the use of somatic cell hybrid panels is an efficient way to assign ESTs to human chromosomes.
the human ESTs can be assigned to human chromosomes and that the ESTs are useful for mapping human cDNA sequences.
ESTs can be used to map human genes to specific chromosomes.
